item: The .eml import holds a bounded amount of mail: a file over 36 MiB is skipped unread and counted, the rest is stored in rounds of 64 MiB (audit 0.5.0 A-006, routing 8)
status: shipped, test-verified, browser-unverified for the new result line
summary: POST /api/newsletters/import read every .eml whole into one list. Now _MAX_EML_BYTES (36 MiB, above Gmail/Yahoo 25 MiB and Outlook.com about 34 MB; one parse at the cap holds about 281 MiB) skips an oversize file unread and counts it in tally.skipped_oversize, and messages are stored in rounds under _EML_BATCH_BYTES (64 MiB) so memory is bounded by the round, not the upload (the audit's total byte budget is answered by the batching; the request body spooled to disk is a stated limit). Parse memory measured on synthetic newsletter-shaped messages: about 7.8x the message (1.3 MiB +10, 25.6 MiB +200, 50.9 MiB +397, 101.6 MiB +791). One chrome string x12. The folder-import path (ingest_eml_files, read_bytes) is unchanged and not bounded here.
